name: nf-core/rnaseq
description: BULK RNA-SEQ PIPELINE: alignment (STAR/HISAT2), quantification (Salmon/featureCounts), QC (FastQC/MultiQC). Preprocessing: adapter trimming (Trim Galore/fastp), ribosomal RNA removal and rRNA contamination depletion (SortMeRNA), strandedness auto-detection and inference (handles unknown strandedness automatically). Use for: RNA-seq from any biological condition — disease vs healthy controls, tissue-specific gene expression (lung, liver, brain), treatment response, COVID-19 or other disease patient cohorts. Identifies differentially expressed genes (upregulated and downregulated) via optional DESeq2/edgeR integration. Handles paired-end, single-end, UMI-based, and stranded/unstranded libraries. Outputs: gene expression count matrices ready for differential expression analysis. Automatically removes adapter sequences, ribosomal RNA contamination, and low-quality reads.
annotation: RNA-seq transcript quantification alignment read counts gene expression FASTQ reads bulk RNA-seq BigWig coverage tracks genome browser visualization Arabidopsis thaliana plant mouse human organism species gene counts featureCounts STAR HISAT2 Salmon RSEM
reason: All keywords accurately describe the tools, data types, and applications of the bulk RNA-seq pipeline.

name: nf-core/sarek
description:
RECOMMENDED PIPELINE FOR WGS/WES SOMATIC AND GERMLINE VARIANT CALLING.

Somatic calling (tumor-normal or tumor-only): Mutect2, Strelka2, Manta, ASCAT (CNV), DeepSomatic; tumor mutational burden (TMB); MSI detection. Use for: somatic mutations from breast cancer, lung cancer, or any tumor-normal paired WGS/WES; cancer genomics; CNV/SV detection.

Germline calling: HaplotypeCaller, DeepVariant, Strelka2 germline, Manta; rare disease SNP/indel calling from WGS/WES. Use for: healthy volunteer WGS, family trio analysis, germline SNP/indel calling, rare disease cohort.

Supports Sentieon-licensed accelerated GATK tools (Sentieon TNscope, DNAscope) as drop-in replacements for Mutect2 and HaplotypeCaller.

Input: FASTQ or BAM, single-sample or paired tumor-normal. Reference: hg38/GRCh38 or hg19/GRCh37. Steps: FastQC → BWA-MEM2 → MarkDuplicates → BQSR → variant calling → GATK filtering → VEP/snpEff annotation.

name: nf-core/differentialabundance
description: Requires pre-computed gene/transcript count matrix as input. Does NOT process raw FASTQ files (use nf-core/rnaseq for that). Downstream differential abundance/expression analysis starting from a pre-computed count matrix. Input: gene count matrix (from nf-core/rnaseq, DESeq2, STAR, featureCounts, etc.) OR h5ad AnnData files from scRNA-seq (Seurat, scanpy). Supports single-cell RNA-seq h5ad input with cell type annotation and per-cluster or per-condition comparisons. Performs: differential expression (DESeq2, edgeR, limma-voom), gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA, fgsea), volcano plots, heatmaps, pathway analysis (MSigDB, KEGG, Reactome), PCA/MDS, contrasts between conditions/treatment groups. Use this when you already have a counts table or annotated h5ad and need DE stats, GSEA, or pathway enrichment. Handles both bulk RNA-seq count matrices and pre-processed single-cell count data. Use when you already have a count matrix or h5ad and want to find enriched pathways, enriched pathways in disease condition, identify genes upregulated in disease vs control, treatment vs untreated enrichment, pathway enrichment analysis, GSEA from counts table. Typical question: 'I have a counts table — which pathways are enriched in the disease condition?' Also used for: Affymetrix microarray differential expression analysis from CEL files (after RMA/vsn normalization to count matrix), proteomics differential abundance from MaxQuant or Proteome Discoverer output.
annotation: differential abundance analysis DESeq2 edgeR limma GSEA gene set enrichment volcano plot count matrix Salmon quantification RNA-seq transcriptomics Affymetrix microarray CEL files expression microarray differential expression CEL file preprocessing limma

name: Wgs Germline Gatk
description: WGS Germline Variant Calling — GATK4 Best Practices. 14-step pipeline: FastQC → fastp → BWA-MEM2 → MarkDuplicates → BQSR → HaplotypeCaller → GenotypeGVCFs → VQSR → SnpEff. Input: FASTQ reads or SRA accession (e.g. SRR, ERR, DRR), reference genome (hg38/GRCh38, hg19/GRCh37, mm10). Outputs: annotated germline VCF, BQSR-recalibrated BAM, duplicate-mark metrics, MultiQC HTML. Callers: GATK HaplotypeCaller (default), DeepVariant, FreeBayes. Supports trio/family calling, VQSR filtering, targeted WES with interval BED. BioMate-curated with full parameter schema, SRA auto-fetch, and genome S3 reference injection. Use for germline single-sample, family trio, or population genetics variant calling of inherited disease. NOT for somatic/tumor samples — use nf-core/sarek for cancer.
annotation: WGS Germline Variant Calling — GATK4 Best Practices GATK4 (Apache 2.0 open-source) is fully installable via conda/Docker/Singularity. Alternative callers: DeepVariant (Google), Strelka2 (Illumina), FreeBayes (open-source). Pipeline steps: 1.  FastQC           — raw read quality control 2.  fastp            — adapter trimming and quality filtering 3.  BWA-MEM2         — alignment to reference genome (hg38/GRCh37) 4.  Samtools sort    — coordinate sort the BAM 5.  MarkDuplicates   — GATK4 MarkDupl
reason: Strelka2 is not supported by this workflow; only HaplotypeCaller, DeepVariant, and FreeBayes are available callers.

Chain: nlmixr2_population_pk → exposure_response_modeling → phase2_dose_justification. Fitting: scipy.optimize.curve_fit (LM/TRR) + bootstrap CI (n=200 replicates). Outputs ec50_uM, emax_pct, hill coefficient, R², and 95% CI bounds. Fixed-Emax mode available when Emax is pre-specified (--emax_fixed). Identifiability check: warns when AUC_max/EC50 < 2.0 (sparse data). Input: patient_data_csv (columns: patient_id, AUC_uM_h, effect_pct). Output: er_params.json (ec50_uM, emax_pct, hill, r_squared, 95%CI), er_curve.csv (predicted E-R curve for plotting). References: Holford & Sheiner 1982, FDA E-R Guidance 2023.
